lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational numbers can be represented in many equivalent ways
lessons.lesson_focus: Build perfect squares from dot/area visuals; relate squares and roots as inverse; estimate √n between consecutive integers; spot patterns.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational numbers can be represented in many equivalent ways
lessons.lesson_focus: Square two-digit numbers via (40+3)²; apply to tiled-floor area/perimeter problems.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Numbers with repeated factors can be expressed using exponential notation
lessons.lesson_focus: Factor trees and repeated prime division; express n as products of prime powers; build fluency with powers of 2, 3, 5.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Numbers with repeated factors can be expressed using exponential notation
lessons.lesson_focus: Find LCM and HCF by comparing prime factorisations. Timetable/packaging contexts.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational numbers can be represented in many equivalent ways
lessons.lesson_focus: Powers of 10 notation; sequence 10, 100, 1000 ↔ 10¹, 10², 10³; expanded notation using place value.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational numbers can be represented in many equivalent ways
lessons.lesson_focus: Equivalent fractions via common multiples, fraction wall, number line; simplify using common divisors.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational numbers can be represented in many equivalent ways
lessons.lesson_focus: Convert between fraction, decimal, percentage. Benchmark equivalences (¼, ½, ¾, ⅛, tenths).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational numbers can be represented in many equivalent ways
lessons.lesson_focus: Locate positive and negative fractions/mixed numerals on number line, including asymmetric intervals.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational numbers can be approximated to support judgements of magnitude and reasonableness
lessons.lesson_focus: Round decimals to specified accuracy; check reasonableness via estimation. Finance/renovation contexts.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The inverse relationships between addition and subtraction and multiplication and division can be used to add, subtract, multiply or divide rational numbers
lessons.lesson_focus: Add and subtract fractions and decimals using rectangular arrays, algebra tiles, partitioning.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Multiplying a positive number by a number greater than 0 and less than 1 results in a smaller number
lessons.lesson_focus: Multiply and divide fractions and decimals. Conceptual models first (fraction walls, arrays), then procedure.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The inverse relationships between addition and subtraction and multiplication and division can be used to add, subtract, multiply or divide rational numbers
lessons.lesson_focus: Strategic choice between fraction, decimal, percentage forms for efficient calculation (e.g. 12.5% × 96 as ⅛ × 96).
lessons.practice_style: Option B: calc lesson with strategic I Do

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The inverse relationships between addition and subtraction and multiplication and division can be used to add, subtract, multiply or divide rational numbers
lessons.lesson_focus: Find a percentage of a quantity (e.g. 15% of $80). Foundational for N09 modelling.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The inverse relationships between addition and subtraction and multiplication and division can be used to add, subtract, multiply or divide rational numbers
lessons.lesson_focus: < and > with positive/negative integers; language work (magnitude, difference, sign); ordering on number line.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The inverse relationships between addition and subtraction and multiplication and division can be used to add, subtract, multiply or divide rational numbers
lessons.lesson_focus: Add and subtract integers using number-line model; apply to lifts/altitude/sea-level modelling.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Fractions, percentages, ratios and rates are different ways of representing a proportional relationship between quantities
lessons.lesson_focus: Ratios as quantitative comparison of groups; part-part vs part-whole; connection to fractions.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Fractions, percentages, ratios and rates are different ways of representing a proportional relationship between quantities
lessons.lesson_focus: Divide a quantity in a given ratio. Applied contexts: money, mixtures, concentrations.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Mathematical modelling can be used to represent and analyse financial and other real-world situations and support informed decision-making
lessons.lesson_focus: Modelling proportional contexts: attendance, voting, land use. Includes First Nations grain-belt comparison.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Mathematical modelling can be used to represent and analyse financial and other real-world situations and support informed decision-making
lessons.lesson_focus: Financial modelling: profit/loss/% profit on fundraiser scenarios.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Algebraic expressions can be represented in infinitely many different but equivalent ways
lessons.lesson_focus: Introduce variable as a letter representing a number; notation conventions (3x = 3×x, no × symbol); distinguish 3x+4 from 3(x+4); generalise from arithmetic patterns like 7+7+7 = 3×7.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Algebraic expressions can be represented in infinitely many different but equivalent ways
lessons.lesson_focus: Translate worded statements into algebraic expressions; 'think of a number' puzzles; vocab work.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Patterns and relationships between variables can be described algebraically and graphed to solve problems and support inferences
lessons.lesson_focus: Evaluate single- and multi-variable expressions; emphasis on order of operations and negative substitutions.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Patterns and relationships between variables can be described algebraically and graphed to solve problems and support inferences
lessons.lesson_focus: Substitute into A=l×w, AFL p=6g+b, target heart rate, wages W=b+1.5hr, density d=m/v.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The commutative and associative properties apply to addition and multiplication, but not to subtraction and division
lessons.lesson_focus: Identify like terms; combine using commutative/associative properties; algebra-tile visuals; distinguish x and x² as different objects.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The distributive property of multiplication over addition and subtraction can be used to support efficient calculation
lessons.lesson_focus: Expand single brackets; area-model visualisation first; 3(x+4) = 3x+12; efficient arithmetic via 7×98 = 7(100−2).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Patterns and relationships between variables can be described algebraically and graphed to solve problems and support inferences
lessons.lesson_focus: Equation as truth statement; solving = finding the value that makes it true; verify candidate solutions by substitution.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Patterns and relationships between variables can be described algebraically and graphed to solve problems and support inferences
lessons.lesson_focus: Function-machine backtracking and balance-scale models; step-by-step reasoning before going algebraic.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Patterns and relationships between variables can be described algebraically and graphed to solve problems and support inferences
lessons.lesson_focus: Solve ax+b=c algebraically using inverse operations; verify every solution by substitution.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Patterns and relationships between variables can be described algebraically and graphed to solve problems and support inferences
lessons.lesson_focus: Build table from visually growing pattern; describe relationship; generalise to rule; use rule to find later terms.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Patterns and relationships between variables can be described algebraically and graphed to solve problems and support inferences
lessons.lesson_focus: Plot ordered pairs from table on Cartesian plane; linear rules produce straight lines; function machines as input-output generators.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Patterns and relationships between variables can be described algebraically and graphed to solve problems and support inferences
lessons.lesson_focus: Interpret authentic-data graphs (temperature, electricity, travel, pouring rates); read values; identify features; match stories to shapes.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Patterns and relationships between variables can be described algebraically and graphed to solve problems and support inferences
lessons.lesson_focus: Reactive tables to vary inputs in formulas (V=lwh, d=st); describe effect of systematic variation.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Measurable attributes of 2-dimensional shapes and 3-dimensional objects can be determined based on the known properties of the shape or solid
lessons.lesson_focus: Derive area of a triangle as half an appropriate rectangle (½×base×height); identify the perpendicular height (not just any side); calculate areas of acute, obtuse and right-angled triangles.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Measurable attributes of 2-dimensional shapes and 3-dimensional objects can be determined based on the known properties of the shape or solid
lessons.lesson_focus: Derive A=base×height for parallelograms by re-arranging into a rectangle; identify the perpendicular height; shade-sail and tiling cost problems.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Measurable attributes of 2-dimensional shapes and 3-dimensional objects can be determined based on the known properties of the shape or solid
lessons.lesson_focus: Build rectangular prisms from unit cubes; derive V=l×w×h; apply to high-rise volume (floor area × number of floors); convert between cm³, m³ and capacity (mL, L).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Measurable attributes of 2-dimensional shapes and 3-dimensional objects can be determined based on the known properties of the shape or solid
lessons.lesson_focus: Generalise to V = cross-section area × length for any right prism; calculate volumes of triangular prisms; predict-and-test cross-section reasoning.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: In any circle, the ratio of the circumference to the diameter is always the same and is represented by the number pi (π)
lessons.lesson_focus: Identify and label centre, radius, diameter, chord and circumference; use the relationship d=2r; First Nations Australians' use of circles in basketry, symbols and architecture.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: In any circle, the ratio of the circumference to the diameter is always the same and is represented by the number pi (π)
lessons.lesson_focus: Measure circumference and diameter of round objects with string; record C÷d; observe the constant ratio ≈ π; historical approximations of π from Egypt, Babylon, Greece, India and China.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Parallel and intersecting lines have properties that can be used to deduce relationships between the angles formed
lessons.lesson_focus: Construct parallel lines; identify corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles when a transversal crosses parallel lines; calculate unknown angles using these relationships.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Parallel and intersecting lines have properties that can be used to deduce relationships between the angles formed
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply parallel-line angle reasoning to real contexts: scissor lifts, folding umbrellas, cherry pickers; justify each step with the angle property used; exterior-angle of a triangle.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Parallel and intersecting lines have properties that can be used to deduce relationships between the angles formed
lessons.lesson_focus: Demonstrate that interior angles of a triangle sum to 180° (tearing-and-arranging); calculate unknown angles in triangles; connect to parallel-line angle properties.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Parallel and intersecting lines have properties that can be used to deduce relationships between the angles formed
lessons.lesson_focus: Decompose polygons into triangles to derive interior angle sum (n−2)×180; calculate interior angles of regular polygons; solve for unknown angles in irregular polygons.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Measurable attributes of 2-dimensional shapes and 3-dimensional objects can be determined based on the known properties of the shape or solid
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply ratios to real contexts: concrete mixing, salad dressing, paint colour mixing, golden ratio in design; investigate how First Nations Australians' knowledges inform pharmaceutical and toxin development.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Geometrical transformations of points and 2-dimensional shapes can be represented on a Cartesian plane
lessons.lesson_focus: Translate points and shapes on the Cartesian plane by a vector; reflect across the x-axis and y-axis; record coordinates before and after; observe that two reflections can give a translation.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Geometrical transformations of points and 2-dimensional shapes can be represented on a Cartesian plane
lessons.lesson_focus: Rotate shapes about a given point (90°, 180°, 270° clockwise/anticlockwise); combine translations, reflections and rotations to create patterns and tessellations.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Variation in data can be measured and used to describe and compare data sets
lessons.lesson_focus: Calculate mean, median, mode and range from a list of values and from a dot plot; understand what each measure tells us about the data; recognise that different data sets can share the same measure of central tendency.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Variation in data can be measured and used to describe and compare data sets
lessons.lesson_focus: Compare mean and median for skewed vs symmetric data; explain how outliers affect each summary statistic; choose mean or median to justify a claim; analyse continuous measurement data from a science experiment.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Data can be organised and represented in different ways to inform, justify and persuade conclusions
lessons.lesson_focus: Construct ordered stem-and-leaf plots from a class data set (e.g. heights in cm); read the median, mode and range directly from the plot; build split stem-and-leaf plots to compare groups.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Variation in data can be measured and used to describe and compare data sets
lessons.lesson_focus: Describe distribution shape using positive skew, negative skew, symmetric and bi-modal; locate the mean and median on each shape; identify outliers and explain their effect on the comparison of two data sets.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Data can be organised and represented in different ways to inform, justify and persuade conclusions
lessons.lesson_focus: Plan and conduct a full statistical investigation: pose a question, collect or source data, summarise with appropriate measures, interpret findings; example contexts include reaction times (teen vs adult), a STEM design improvement, or secondary data from the Reconciliation Barometer.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational and irrational numbers can be expressed and represented in different forms depending on context and purpose
lessons.lesson_focus: Distinguish rational from irrational numbers; introduce π and √2 as familiar examples; locate irrational numbers on the real number line between consecutive rationals (e.g. 3.141 < π < 3.142); connect the constant ratio C÷d to π.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational and irrational numbers can be expressed and represented in different forms depending on context and purpose
lessons.lesson_focus: Encounter irrationals through measurement — diagonal of a unit square, hypotenuse from a known area, ratios of A0/A1/A2/A3/A4 paper sizes, golden ratio in art and design; historical approximations of π across cultures.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Exponential laws describe patterns in operations involving exponential notation enabling efficient calculations
lessons.lesson_focus: Build the product rule aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ and quotient rule aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ from expanded form; apply with positive integer exponents; emphasise that bases must match.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Exponential laws describe patterns in operations involving exponential notation enabling efficient calculations
lessons.lesson_focus: Derive (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐ×ⁿ from expanded form; justify a⁰ = 1 using the quotient law (3⁴/3⁴ = 1 = 3⁰); build fluency with the four exponent laws so far.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Exponential laws describe patterns in operations involving exponential notation enabling efficient calculations
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply multiple exponent laws in succession; cube-enlargement context (2 cm cube to 6 cm cube, volume increases by factor 27 = 3³); check that bases match before combining.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational and irrational numbers can be expressed and represented in different forms depending on context and purpose
lessons.lesson_focus: Convert fractions to decimal forms; predict terminating vs recurring from the prime factorisation of the denominator (only 2s and 5s gives terminating); use dot notation for recurring decimals.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational and irrational numbers can be expressed and represented in different forms depending on context and purpose
lessons.lesson_focus: Establish sign rules for multiplication and division of integers using patterns; calculate products and quotients of signed integers; recognise the effect of sign in (-1)ⁿ.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational and irrational numbers can be expressed and represented in different forms depending on context and purpose
lessons.lesson_focus: Combine all four operations with positive and negative fractions and decimals; use commutative/associative regrouping for efficient calculation; flexible choice between fraction and decimal forms.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Mathematical modelling can be used to represent and solve practical problems, including in financial contexts, using rational numbers and percentages
lessons.lesson_focus: Calculate mark-ups, discounts and GST as percentage change; one-step multiplier method (×1.10 for 10% up); apply to multi-period contexts such as market trends, population change and recycling rates.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Mathematical modelling can be used to represent and solve practical problems, including in financial contexts, using rational numbers and percentages
lessons.lesson_focus: Model real contexts using positive and negative rational quantities — daily temperature changes, sea depths and altitudes, average-temperature differences across seasons.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Mathematical modelling can be used to represent and solve practical problems, including in financial contexts, using rational numbers and percentages
lessons.lesson_focus: Use marginal tax tables to compute personal income tax at various income levels; calculate the overall percentage of income paid as tax; compare effective tax rates across incomes.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Equivalent algebraic expressions and solutions to equations can be determined by applying properties of mathematical operations and numbers
lessons.lesson_focus: Simplify expressions by collecting like terms with integer coefficients, including multi-variable expressions like 5m + 10n + 3m − 4n; use algebra tiles to justify each step; identity and inverse properties named explicitly.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Equivalent algebraic expressions and solutions to equations can be determined by applying properties of mathematical operations and numbers
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply the distributive property to expand a(b + c) and a(b − c); use area models and algebra tiles to justify; expressions such as 3(a − b) = 3a − 3b and −2(x + 5) = −2x − 10.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Equivalent algebraic expressions and solutions to equations can be determined by applying properties of mathematical operations and numbers
lessons.lesson_focus: Reverse expanding by identifying the highest common factor; rewrite expressions like 2x + 4 as 2(x + 2) and 6a − 9 as 3(2a − 3); confirm by re-expanding.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Equivalent algebraic expressions and solutions to equations can be determined by applying properties of mathematical operations and numbers
lessons.lesson_focus: Coordinate expanding, simplifying and collecting like terms in multi-step problems like 5(m + 2n) + 3m − 4n; write equivalent forms strategically; verify by substituting a test value.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Linear relations between two variables can be represented algebraically and graphically, leading to generalised patterns and conjectures
lessons.lesson_focus: Recognise linearity from a constant first difference in a table of values; complete tables from rules; plot ordered pairs and verify points lie on a straight line.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Linear relations between two variables can be represented algebraically and graphically, leading to generalised patterns and conjectures
lessons.lesson_focus: Graph lines of the form x = a and y = a; graph and shade inequality regions x ≤ a, x > a, y ≤ a, y > a on the Cartesian plane; recognise the conventions for solid and dashed boundary lines.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Linear relations between two variables can be represented algebraically and graphically, leading to generalised patterns and conjectures
lessons.lesson_focus: Solve ax + b = c using inverse operations; verify solutions by substitution; extend to two-step rearrangements with both positive and negative coefficients of x.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Linear relations between two variables can be represented algebraically and graphically, leading to generalised patterns and conjectures
lessons.lesson_focus: Solve ax + b < c and ax + b > c using inverse operations (a > 0); represent solutions on a number line; check with a test value; graphical interpretation as the region where the line is above or below c.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Linear relations between two variables can be represented algebraically and graphically, leading to generalised patterns and conjectures
lessons.lesson_focus: Solve equations like 3x + 7 = 6x − 9 by collecting variables on one side; verify by substitution and visualise graphically as the intersection of two lines.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Linear relations between two variables can be represented algebraically and graphically, leading to generalised patterns and conjectures
lessons.lesson_focus: Model contexts with linear functions — taxi fares with flag-fall fee, water tank drainage, trade quotes with call-out fees; interpret slope as rate of change and y-intercept as starting value; check validity (e.g. once tank is empty, no more flows).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Linear relations between two variables can be represented algebraically and graphically, leading to generalised patterns and conjectures
lessons.lesson_focus: Use tables of values and graphs to represent pay-rate relationships; calculate weekly earnings from hourly rates including overtime; compare casual and salaried pay structures.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Linear relations between two variables can be represented algebraically and graphically, leading to generalised patterns and conjectures
lessons.lesson_focus: Use graphing software to vary parameters of y = mx + c systematically; form and test conjectures about slope direction and y-intercept; explore integer solutions to 2x + 3y = 48.

lessons.lesson_focus: Extend the Cartesian plane to a three-dimensional coordinate system (x, y, z); locate aircraft and drones using latitude, longitude and altitude; interpret coordinates in multi-storey carparks and play 3D Tic-Tac-Toe.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Valid inferences about populations can be made by drawing conclusions from representative samples
lessons.lesson_focus: Distinguish census from sample; identify when each is feasible or required; weigh the cost/accuracy/practicality trade-offs in survey design with realistic scenarios.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Valid inferences about populations can be made by drawing conclusions from representative samples
lessons.lesson_focus: Recognise sampling bias, response bias and observer bias in real studies (e.g. shopping-centre surveys, online polls); discuss precision and error in digital measurement tools; suggest redesigns to reduce bias.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: A representative sample depends on the nature of the population and the question being considered
lessons.lesson_focus: Compare simple random, systematic, stratified, quota, cluster, convenience and judgement sampling; match the method to the population structure; define probabilistic terms — random, sample space, sample, sample distribution.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: A representative sample depends on the nature of the population and the question being considered
lessons.lesson_focus: Use simulations to draw repeated samples from a known population; observe how mean, median and range vary between samples of the same size; investigate the effect of adding or removing data on central tendency and spread.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: A representative sample depends on the nature of the population and the question being considered
lessons.lesson_focus: Compare the variation of sample statistics for small vs large samples; relate to reliability of inferences; use relative frequencies from historical data; investigate First Nations Ranger Group sampling for biodiversity tracking.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Valid inferences about populations can be made by drawing conclusions from representative samples
lessons.lesson_focus: Plan and conduct a full sample-based investigation: pose a question, design the sample, collect data, analyse with appropriate summary statistics, report findings with acknowledgement of uncertainty; example contexts include pandemic-impact electricity data and reconciliation progress.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Complementary events in an experiment are mutually exclusive and together cover all possible outcomes
lessons.lesson_focus: Recognise that P(A) + P(not A) = 1; use the complement to calculate probabilities of events that are not equally likely, including supermarket-promotion and dice contexts (P(not 6) = 5/6).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The sample space for 2 events can be presented diagrammatically in a variety of ways to determine the probabilities of specific outcomes, including compound events
lessons.lesson_focus: Construct two-way tables and Venn diagrams for two events; calculate probabilities involving 'and', exclusive 'or', inclusive 'or' using language precisely; populate tables from word problems.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The sample space for 2 events can be presented diagrammatically in a variety of ways to determine the probabilities of specific outcomes, including compound events
lessons.lesson_focus: Distinguish mutually exclusive events (P(A and B) = 0) from inclusive events; apply Pr(A and B) + Pr(A and not B) + Pr(not A and B) + Pr(not A and not B) = 1; explore the Battendi game from the Ngarrindjeri Peoples.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The sample space for 2 events can be presented diagrammatically in a variety of ways to determine the probabilities of specific outcomes, including compound events
lessons.lesson_focus: Use digital random-number generators to simulate compound events; compare experimental probabilities with theoretical predictions; investigate the dice-difference experiment to see which differences occur most often.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational and irrational numbers can be represented in many forms, including on a number line, and can be used to find exact and approximate values
lessons.lesson_focus: Classify numbers in the real number hierarchy — natural, integer, rational, irrational; locate rationals and surds like √2 on the number line using geometric construction; represent solutions to linear inequalities of the form ax + b < c as intervals on a number line.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Rational and irrational numbers can be represented in many forms, including on a number line, and can be used to find exact and approximate values
lessons.lesson_focus: Substitute real numbers into formulas including A = πr² and the distance formula; choose between exact form (in terms of π or with surds) and decimal approximations as the context demands; solve budgeting problems with positive and negative rationals.

lessons.mapping_note: Partial - this lesson covers the product, quotient and power-of-a-power laws with numerical bases
lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Expressions involving exponent notation with integer or variable bases can be simplified or represented differently using the law of exponents
lessons.lesson_focus: Derive the product, quotient and power-of-a-power laws from first principles by counting repeated factors; worked examples 2^3 x 2^4, 7^5 / 7^2, (5^2)^3, (a^2)^3; Stretch/Mastery combine two or three laws and push to impractical-to-evaluate exponents.

lessons.mapping_note: Partial - this lesson covers the zero index and negative integer exponents
lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Expressions involving exponent notation with integer or variable bases can be simplified or represented differently using the law of exponents
lessons.lesson_focus: Descending-powers pattern (2^3...2^-2) forces 2^0=1 and reciprocal negatives; worked examples 5^-3, (1/3)^-2, x^0; Always/Sometimes/Never targets the x^0=0 and negative-index-means-negative misconceptions.

lessons.mapping_note: Partial - this lesson covers applying the exponent laws to algebraic terms with variable bases
lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Expressions involving exponent notation with integer or variable bases can be simplified or represented differently using the law of exponents
lessons.lesson_focus: Same laws on algebraic terms - coefficient and variable parts handled separately; worked examples 3x^2 x 4x^3, 12a^5/3a^2, (2x)^3, (2xy)^3/(xy^4); coefficient-vs-exponent confusion targeted explicitly.

lessons.mapping_note: Partial - this lesson covers expanding binomial products
lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The parameters of quadratics and other functions determine the features of the related graph and can be adjusted depending on the purpose, context and application
lessons.lesson_focus: Expand (x+a)(x+b) via area model and distributive property; recognise x^2+(a+b)x+ab pattern.

lessons.mapping_note: Partial - this lesson covers the special products perfect squares and difference of two squares
lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The parameters of quadratics and other functions determine the features of the related graph and can be adjusted depending on the purpose, context and application
lessons.lesson_focus: Perfect-square (x+a)^2 and difference-of-two-squares (x-a)(x+a)=x^2-a^2 patterns.

lessons.mapping_note: Partial - this lesson covers factorising monic quadratic expressions
lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The parameters of quadratics and other functions determine the features of the related graph and can be adjusted depending on the purpose, context and application
lessons.lesson_focus: Factorise x^2+mx+n via the integer pair multiplying to n and adding to m; verify by re-expanding.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: On a Cartesian plane, the coordinates of 2 distinct points can be used to determine a range of measures of their orientation in relation to each other
lessons.lesson_focus: Use Pythagoras' theorem to derive the distance formula d = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]; find the midpoint of a line segment using the average of coordinates; apply both to coordinate-geometry problems.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: On a Cartesian plane, the coordinates of 2 distinct points can be used to determine a range of measures of their orientation in relation to each other
lessons.lesson_focus: Use gradients to test whether two lines are parallel (m₁ = m₂) or perpendicular (m₁ × m₂ = −1); apply to coordinate-geometry problems; investigate gradients in real contexts using superimposed photos.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The parameters of quadratics and other functions determine the features of the related graph and can be adjusted depending on the purpose, context and application
lessons.lesson_focus: Identify quadratic relations from tables of values (constant second difference); plot quadratic functions y = x², y = x² + c, y = ax²; describe features — turning point, axis of symmetry, y-intercept, direction of opening; explore with graphing software.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The parameters of quadratics and other functions determine the features of the related graph and can be adjusted depending on the purpose, context and application
lessons.lesson_focus: Connect the factorised form y = (x − a)(x − b) with x-intercepts at a and b via the null factor law; sketch quadratic graphs given their factorised form; recognise when a quadratic has no real x-intercepts; relate moon-phase illumination to a quadratic-shaped curve.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The parameters of quadratics and other functions determine the features of the related graph and can be adjusted depending on the purpose, context and application
lessons.lesson_focus: Solve monic quadratic equations x² + bx + c = 0 algebraically by factorising and applying the null factor law; verify solutions by substitution and compare with graphical solutions; include the x² = a case with solutions ±√a.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Mathematical modelling can be used to represent and solve problems involving changes, including financial contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Model practical contexts using linear functions — cooking with resting times, water tank drainage, trade quotes with call-out fees, change-modelling for temperature and speed; interpret slope and y-intercept in context; check validity of the model.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Mathematical modelling can be used to represent and solve problems involving changes, including financial contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Model practical contexts using quadratic functions — projectile paths, parabolic mirrors and satellite dishes, area problems where one dimension is a linear function of another; identify and interpret turning point and intercepts in context; First Nations hunting techniques as a quadratic modelling context.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Mathematical modelling can be used to represent and solve problems involving changes, including financial contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Choose between linear and quadratic models for financial contexts — combinations of purchases under a budget, profit/loss curves, trade quotes; justify the choice with reference to constant first-difference (linear) or constant second-difference (quadratic) patterns in data.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The parameters of quadratics and other functions determine the features of the related graph and can be adjusted depending on the purpose, context and application
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate transformations of the linear graph y = x — vertical enlargement (y = 2x), vertical compression (y = x/2), reflection (y = −x), vertical translation (y = 2x − 1); formalise the slope-intercept form y = mx + c.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The parameters of quadratics and other functions determine the features of the related graph and can be adjusted depending on the purpose, context and application
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate transformations of the parabola y = x² in completed-square form y = a(x − h)² + k; identify how a controls dilation/reflection, h controls horizontal translation, k controls vertical translation; locate the turning point at (h, k).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The parameters of quadratics and other functions determine the features of the related graph and can be adjusted depending on the purpose, context and application
lessons.lesson_focus: Explore other function families using digital tools — reciprocal y = 1/x, square root y = √x, cubic y = x³, exponential y = 2ˣ and y = (1/2)ˣ; identify key features and pattern-spot the effect of parameter changes.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Spatial relationships in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions can be quantified using appropriate units to solve problems in various contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Use nets to derive surface-area formulas for rectangular and triangular right prisms; calculate surface area by summing component face areas; verify by re-drawing the net in a different layout.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Spatial relationships in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions can be quantified using appropriate units to solve problems in various contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply formulas V = πr²h and SA = 2πr² + 2πrh for a cylinder; derive the curved-surface area by unrolling the cylinder into a rectangle of dimensions 2πr by h; can-cooler material problems.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Spatial relationships in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions can be quantified using appropriate units to solve problems in various contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate optimisation problems — prisms with the same volume but different surface areas; can-cooler material minimisation; conjecture and test which shapes give the smallest surface area for a given volume; First Nations objects/technologies as SA-volume contexts.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Spatial relationships in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions can be quantified using appropriate units to solve problems in various contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Convert numbers between standard form and scientific notation a × 10ⁿ where 1 ≤ a < 10; represent very large quantities (4.6 × 10⁹ for the age of the Earth) and very small ones (5.68 × 10⁻²¹ for the mass of a sugar molecule); connect to SI prefixes from pico- to tera-.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Spatial relationships in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions can be quantified using appropriate units to solve problems in various contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Multiply and divide numbers in scientific notation using exponent laws; estimate orders of magnitude for products and quotients; record measurements to an accuracy appropriate to the measuring instrument (cylinder vs pipette).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Spatial relationships in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions can be quantified using appropriate units to solve problems in various contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometric ratios together in spatial problems — surveying, ramp design, building diagonals; multi-step problems where Pythagoras gives one side and trig gives an angle, or vice versa; distance between Cartesian points as a Pythagoras application.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Spatial relationships in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions can be quantified using appropriate units to solve problems in various contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate the effect of scale factor k on area (× k²) and volume (× k³) for similar figures; apply to scaled models, photographs and original objects; estimate actual measurements from images using proportional reasoning.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Spatial relationships in 1, 2 and 3 dimensions can be quantified using appropriate units to solve problems in various contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Integrate similarity, Pythagoras' theorem, rates and algebra in extended problems — Biltmore stick design for measuring tree height and diameter; the triangle inequality and related conjectures for acute/obtuse triangles; minimal information sets to determine a triangle.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Calculations are affected by sources of error and should be interpreted in the context of the problem
lessons.lesson_focus: Calculate absolute error |measured − exact|, relative error (absolute error ÷ exact value), and percentage error; use absolute value notation in the error formula; recognise that all measurements are estimates with associated uncertainty.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Calculations are affected by sources of error and should be interpreted in the context of the problem
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply error analysis to real contexts — percentage error in predicted vs actual event attendance; budgeted vs actual expenditure; give suitable lower and upper bounds for measurement values in practical contexts.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Mathematical modelling can be used to represent and solve problems involving proportion, rates, ratios and scale, including in financial contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Model direct-proportion situations — pro rata pay rates, currency exchange, multiple quotes for a job, Hooke's law from physics; investigate situations where proportion is not maintained (image editing/distortion); building and construction standards for staircases and escalators.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Mathematical modelling can be used to represent and solve problems involving proportion, rates, ratios and scale, including in financial contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Model applied rate contexts — density, birth rate, flow rate, heart rate; vehicle acceleration and deceleration; explore fire-spread rate techniques in First Nations Australians' land management under varying fuel types, wind, temperature and humidity.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Trigonometric ratios are an application of the property of similarity for right-angled triangles
lessons.lesson_focus: Identify and label the hypotenuse, the side opposite a given angle, and the side adjacent to a given angle in any right-angled triangle; recognise that 'opposite' and 'adjacent' depend on the chosen reference angle; the hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Trigonometric ratios are an application of the property of similarity for right-angled triangles
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate nested similar right-angled triangles with a fixed acute angle; measure side ratios systematically and observe that opposite/hypotenuse, adjacent/hypotenuse and opposite/adjacent stay constant for that angle; connect to the unit-hypotenuse triangle.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Trigonometric ratios are an application of the property of similarity for right-angled triangles
lessons.lesson_focus: Define sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse, cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse, tan θ = opposite/adjacent; read sin, cos, tan values from a calculator for any acute angle; connect tan θ to the gradient of a line passing through the origin.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Trigonometric ratios are an application of the property of similarity for right-angled triangles
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply the enlargement transformation to shapes using a centre of enlargement and a scale factor; recognise that corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are in a fixed ratio; solve enlargement problems using similarity.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Trigonometric ratios are an application of the property of similarity for right-angled triangles
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate how enlargement by scale factor k affects area (× k²) and volume (× k³); compare side lengths, areas and volumes of similar squares and cubes for k = 2, 3, and fractional k; generalise the pattern to any similar 2D and 3D shape.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Trigonometric ratios are an application of the property of similarity for right-angled triangles
lessons.lesson_focus: Design an algorithm (flow chart or pseudocode) that applies the triangle inequality to determine whether three given lengths can form a triangle; design an alternative algorithm to generate Pythagorean triples systematically.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Trigonometric ratios are an application of the property of similarity for right-angled triangles
lessons.lesson_focus: Design an algorithm using pseudocode or a flow chart to construct or bisect an angle with compass and straightedge; describe each step precisely; test for correctness on multiple cases; extend to algorithms for animated geometric constructions or visual proofs.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Statistical reports provide data and analysis to support conclusions and acknowledge the strength of the evidence
lessons.lesson_focus: Analyse statistical reports from media and government sources — link claims to the displays and statistics that support them; investigate how data was obtained, sample size and representativeness; environmental and international examples including Australia–Asia trade statistics and public-opinion surveys.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Sampling methods can affect and bias the results of data collection
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate how different sampling methods and choices of representation can support a particular viewpoint or mislead the reader; analyse infographics for visual bias; consider the impact of decreased landline usage on survey data; explore potential cultural bias in reports about First Nations Australians.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Different representations of data distributions can be used to compare features such as centre, shape and spread
lessons.lesson_focus: Compare two data sets using parallel dot plots and back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots; describe similarities and differences in centre, spread and shape using terms like positive skew, negative skew, symmetric, bi-modal.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Different representations of data distributions can be used to compare features such as centre, shape and spread
lessons.lesson_focus: Construct and interpret grouped histograms — age-grouped health data such as lung cancer, leukaemia, stroke; describe distribution shape and explain its connection to the relative positions of mean and median; explore Closing the Gap report data.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Different representations of data distributions can be used to compare features such as centre, shape and spread
lessons.lesson_focus: Match the data display to the data type — categorical (bar chart, stacked bar chart) vs numerical (histogram, dot plot, stem-and-leaf); compare displays of the same data using mean, median and range; critique infographic choices for the statistical questions they purport to answer.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Statistical reports provide data and analysis to support conclusions and acknowledge the strength of the evidence
lessons.lesson_focus: Plan and conduct a full statistical investigation using primary or secondary data sources such as the ABS — pose a question, collect or extract data, choose displays, analyse, report findings with explicit acknowledgement of uncertainty; investigation contexts include consumer spending habits, tropical-fruit plantation siting, and reconciliation data.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The likelihood of an event occurring can be affected by another event that has already taken place
lessons.lesson_focus: Use lists and arrays to record outcomes of two-step compound experiments — the Heads and Tails game, drawing two team leaders from a class; calculate probabilities by counting favourable outcomes over total outcomes.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The likelihood of an event occurring can be affected by another event that has already taken place
lessons.lesson_focus: Use tree diagrams to represent two- and three-step compound events; contrast experiments with and without replacement (e.g. drawing 3 cards from a deck); multiply probabilities along each path and sum across paths for the target event.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Theoretical probabilities are based on the characteristics of an experiment and can be used to predict relative frequencies of experimental data
lessons.lesson_focus: Use relative frequencies from historical or experimental data to estimate probabilities of events; use Venn diagrams and two-way tables to handle events involving 'and', inclusive 'or' (A or B or both), and exclusive 'or' (A or B but not both).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The probability of compound events is related to the probability of the associated simple events and can be calculated in the context of the experiment
lessons.lesson_focus: Use digital random-number tools to simulate compound events; compare experimental probability with theoretical predictions; contrast results from experiments that differ only by being with or without replacement; explore the First Nations Gorri game from across Australia as a repeated-trial context.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Using approximations rather than exact values affects the accuracy of results in both single and multiple calculations
lessons.lesson_focus: Compare the effect of truncation versus rounding on a single calculation; recognise that exact form (surds, π, fractions) preserves accuracy where decimal approximations introduce error; identify the interval between consecutive integers containing a given irrational.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Using approximations rather than exact values affects the accuracy of results in both single and multiple calculations
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate how rounding errors compound across multiple calculations — area of compound shapes involving circles (π approximations), surface area and volume of compound objects, repeated simple-interest calculations where each cycle's rounding shifts the final balance; quantify the discrepancy from the exact-form answer.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Expand binomial products of the form (ax + b)(cx + d) using the area model and the distributive property; consolidate the perfect-square patterns (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b², and the difference-of-squares (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²; identify when each special pattern applies.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Factorise by extracting the highest common factor first; factorise difference-of-squares a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b); factorise perfect-square trinomials; factorise non-monic quadratics ax² + bx + c using the AC (split-the-middle) method; verify every factorisation by re-expanding.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Rewrite x² + bx + c in completed-square form (x + b/2)² + (c − b²/4); extend to ax² + bx + c by first factorising out a; connect to the perfect-square expansion pattern; interpret the completed-square form geometrically as the turning point of the related parabola y = a(x − h)² + k.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Solve quadratic equations algebraically by factorising, by completing the square, and using the quadratic formula x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/(2a); derive the formula from the completed-square form; recognise when the discriminant indicates no real solutions; choose an efficient method given the form of the equation.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply exponent laws to algebraic expressions involving both positive and negative integer exponents, e.g. (3x²y⁻¹)² ÷ (6x⁻¹y²); rewrite expressions without negative exponents using a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ; solve simple equations of the form aⁿ = b algebraically using the exponent laws.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Solve a pair of simultaneous linear equations by graphing both lines and identifying the intersection point; interpret the intersection in context (e.g. break-even point, point at which two quotes are equal); recognise the three cases — one solution, no solution (parallel lines), infinite solutions (coincident lines).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Solve simultaneous linear equations using the substitution method and the elimination method; choose between methods based on the form of the equations; verify each solution by substitution into both equations; relate the algebraic solution to the graphical intersection point.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Model practical situations with simultaneous equations — comparing two job quotes (fixed call-out plus hourly rate), profit/loss break-even, mixing two priced items to a total budget; communicate solutions in everyday language such as break-even point or point-to-change-providers; explore First Nations Australian children's instructive games (e.g. Weme from the Warlpiri Peoples) and their connection to strategic reasoning.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Graph the solution region for a single linear inequality in two variables (e.g. 2x + 3y < 24); use a test point such as (0, 0) to determine which side of the line to shade; recognise the convention of solid versus dashed boundary lines for ≤/≥ versus </>; test whether a given point satisfies an inequality (extending to non-linear cases like 2y < x²).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Graph systems of two or more linear inequalities and identify the feasible region; find all integer solutions in the feasible region for budget problems such as combinations of movie trips at $12 each and ice-skating sessions at $21 each with an entertainment budget of $150 (12m + 21s ≤ 150); list integer solutions and interpret in context.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Recognise an exponential relation from a table of values by checking whether the ratio between consecutive values of the dependent variable is constant; contrast with the constant first-difference diagnostic for linear and constant second-difference for quadratic; plot y = aˣ for a = 2, 3, ½, ⅓ and describe the family.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Identify the y-intercept (always 1 for y = aˣ), horizontal asymptote (y = 0), domain, range, and whether the function represents growth (a > 1) or decay (0 < a < 1); explore transformations y = aˣ + k and y = aˣ⁻ʰ using graphing software; describe systematic changes in features.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Solve exponential equations by inspection (equating exponents when bases match, e.g. 2ˣ = 32); solve graphically using digital tools (intersection of y = aˣ with y = c); solve using symbolic-manipulation tools; explore First Nations Australian Ranger groups' programs that model feral-versus-native animal populations using exponential equations.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Diagnose the appropriate function family for a context by examining a table of values — linear (constant first difference), quadratic (constant second difference), exponential (constant ratio); apply the diagnostic to data sets from finance, biology and physics; justify the choice and check the model against further data.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Model situations involving constant percentage change — population growth, bacterial growth, radioactive decay; calculate doubling time and half-life; determine the approximate interval over which values of the model lie within a given range; formulate exponential equations for First Nations Australian Ranger native-versus-feral population modelling.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply the compound interest formula A = P(1 + r/n)ⁿᵗ to authentic investment and loan scenarios; compare compound interest with simple interest over the same period; investigate the effect of compounding frequency (annual vs monthly vs daily); use authentic Australian interest rates and discuss real returns adjusted for inflation.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply exponential decay models to carbon dating of First Nations Australians' artefacts and material culture; investigate population modelling for native animals on Country/Place with varying reproductive behaviour; critique the applicability of an exponential model when populations approach environmental carrying capacity.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Use the zoom functionality of graphing tools to systematically refine intervals and approximate intersections of dissimilar functions (e.g. x² = 2ˣ, intersection of a linear function with a quadratic or a circle); compare graphical and algebraic solutions where both are available; recognise that some intersections have no exact closed-form solution.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Recognise x² + y² = 1 as the unit circle centred at the origin; apply transformations — dilation x² + y² = r² (scaling), translation (x − h)² + (y − k)² = r²; locate the centre and radius of any circle written in standard form; sketch transformed circles on the Cartesian plane.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Relationships between variables can be described and modelled by linear, quadratic and exponential functions applied in many contexts including financial ones
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply the bisection algorithm to approximate the x-intercepts of a quadratic such as f(x) = 2x² − 3x − 7; identify intervals on the real number line where a quadratic is positive or negative (sign chart); use a table of values to determine when an exponential growth or decay model exceeds or falls below a given value, e.g. share-price monitoring.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Attributes of 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional objects are described and measured in appropriate standardised units
lessons.lesson_focus: Calculate the surface area of composite solids formed from right prisms and cylinders by considering each component face and identifying hidden internal faces; carefully subtract overlapping regions where solids meet; check answers against a sketched net layout.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Attributes of 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional objects are described and measured in appropriate standardised units
lessons.lesson_focus: Calculate the volume of composite solids by decomposing into right prisms and cylinders, summing component volumes; for hollow composites (e.g. pipe sections), subtract the inner volume from the outer; verify with an alternative decomposition.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Attributes of 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional objects are described and measured in appropriate standardised units
lessons.lesson_focus: Estimate surface area and volume of irregular composite objects in practical contexts; use mathematical modelling to determine the rainfall that can be saved from a roof top and the optimal shape and dimensions for rainwater storage; determine whether to hire extra freezer space for a fundraising event based on volume of ice cream required.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Attributes of 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional objects are described and measured in appropriate standardised units
lessons.lesson_focus: Understand that a logarithmic scale is calibrated in terms of order of magnitude — doubling (×2 per step) or powers of 10; read values from a log-scale axis; identify and interpret data representations using log scales; discuss when a log scale is appropriate (wide range of values, percentage change, exponential growth) versus when a linear scale is preferred.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Attributes of 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional objects are described and measured in appropriate standardised units
lessons.lesson_focus: Interpret real-world logarithmic scales — Richter (earthquake magnitude), decibel (sound intensity), pH (acidity), star apparent magnitude; understand what a one-unit change represents on each scale; investigate dating of First Peoples of Australia's archaeological sites (e.g. Madjedbebe, NT) using scientific notation and measurement-accuracy considerations.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Attributes of 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional objects are described and measured in appropriate standardised units
lessons.lesson_focus: Define angle of elevation as the angle measured upward from the horizontal to a target; define angle of depression similarly downward; apply right-angled trigonometry to find heights and distances; use a clinometer (or simulated app) to measure angles of inclination and determine the height of buildings, flagpoles or trees.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Attributes of 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional objects are described and measured in appropriate standardised units
lessons.lesson_focus: Read and write three-figure bearings (000° to 360° measured clockwise from north); apply right-angled trigonometry to multi-leg navigation problems such as orienteering courses; determine the final bearing and estimate the distance of the closing leg of a route; explore navigation, design of technologies or surveying by First Nations Australians and connections to trigonometric reasoning.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Attributes of 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional objects are described and measured in appropriate standardised units
lessons.lesson_focus: Decompose three-dimensional problems into two-dimensional right-angled triangles; calculate the longest internal diagonal of a rectangular prism using Pythagoras' theorem twice; calculate the angle a diagonal makes with a face; determine the smallest box needed to package an object of given length; use dynamic geometry software for crime-scene reconstruction style problems.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Measurement errors impact the accuracy of results
lessons.lesson_focus: Describe settings where measurement errors impact research results — biased findings, instrumentation limitations; analyse instruments and methods for measurement in investigations (resolution, accuracy, calibration); recognise how systematic versus random error propagates; design improvements that reduce error in a given experimental setup.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Measurement errors impact the accuracy of results
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate scientific measuring techniques applied to First Peoples of Australia and their artefacts — radiocarbon dating, optically stimulated luminescence, genetic sequencing; discuss measurement-error implications for archaeological claims; examine the social impact of measurement errors in cultural-heritage research.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Attributes of 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional objects are described and measured in appropriate standardised units
lessons.lesson_focus: Use plans and elevation drawings to investigate changes to building designs; convert between scale and actual measurements; estimate the scale of an object such as a toy car by measuring one linear dimension and comparing with a known full-size dimension; make decisions about design changes based on scaled measurements.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Attributes of 1-, 2- and 3-dimensional objects are described and measured in appropriate standardised units
lessons.lesson_focus: Analyse and apply scale and ratios in production-prototype contexts including 3D printing; use a 3D printer (or simulation) to produce scaled versions of actual objects; investigate compliance with building codes and standards in design and construction, e.g. tread/riser ratios for escalators in shopping centres.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Situations involving angles, distance and direction can be quantified using geometric properties and theorems
lessons.lesson_focus: Distinguish a practical demonstration (e.g. placing triangles on top of each other to show congruence, tearing-and-arranging interior angles) from a formal proof (a sequence of logically connected statements that establish the result for all cases); recognise the role of assumptions, definitions and previously established theorems in a proof.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Situations involving angles, distance and direction can be quantified using geometric properties and theorems
lessons.lesson_focus: Develop formal proofs involving congruent triangles and angle properties; communicate each proof as a sequence of logically connected statements with justifications drawn from definitions, given information and congruence tests (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS); prove standard results such as the base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Situations involving angles, distance and direction can be quantified using geometric properties and theorems
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply similarity tests in formal proofs and numerical exercises involving plane shapes; use visual proofs to justify solutions; investigate proofs of geometric theorems and apply them to solve spatial problems; use dynamic geometry software to investigate properties such as the shortest path that touches three sides of a rectangle starting and finishing at the same point, and prove the path forms a parallelogram.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Situations involving angles, distance and direction can be quantified using geometric properties and theorems
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate how networks (graphs) can model authentic situations — recognise what the nodes (vertices) represent and what the edges represent; describe the connectedness of a network; tackle the Seven Bridges of Königsberg problem — can each bridge be crossed exactly once? — and connect to the concept of degree of a vertex.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Situations involving angles, distance and direction can be quantified using geometric properties and theorems
lessons.lesson_focus: Represent polyhedra as networks using edges, vertices, and interior and exterior faces; record F, V and E for the five Platonic solids in a table and demonstrate Euler's formula F + V = E + 2 holds; predict F for a polyhedron given E and V; relate the formula to map colouring and planarity.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Situations involving angles, distance and direction can be quantified using geometric properties and theorems
lessons.lesson_focus: Represent authentic situations as network diagrams — social networks, intranet/LAN/wireless networks of a home, electrical wiring, rail or air travel networks (London, Paris, Hong Kong), food webs in a simple ecosystem, metabolic networks; represent First Nations Australians' kinship systems using network diagrams and explore the significance of relationships to Country/Place.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Situations involving angles, distance and direction can be quantified using geometric properties and theorems
lessons.lesson_focus: Apply a computational-thinking approach to problems involving networks — investigate connectedness, coverage and weighted measures (edge weights for distance or cost); design or trace algorithms for choosing the most efficient route on a road network using virtual map software; compare alternative algorithms on the same network.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Situations involving angles, distance and direction can be quantified using geometric properties and theorems
lessons.lesson_focus: Design and make scale models of three-dimensional objects using digital tools (e.g. 3D-printable puzzle components using tessellations); define and decompose spatial problems and create algorithms — for example, a floor plan that limits congestion at checkouts; test algorithms in pseudocode or flow charts; produce self-similar patterns and validate algorithms with multiple test cases; explore geospatial technologies used by First Nations Australians' communities.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Claims and inferences based on data should acknowledge ethical considerations and potential sources of bias
lessons.lesson_focus: Identify potentially misleading representations in the media — graphs with broken axes, scales that do not start at zero, nonlinear scales presented as linear; recognise when data is not related to the claim, not representative of the population, or is being used selectively; investigate the source and size of the sample from which the data was collected and assess whether it is appropriately representative.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Claims and inferences based on data should acknowledge ethical considerations and potential sources of bias
lessons.lesson_focus: Investigate population rates and discuss ethical considerations when presenting infection rates and cases per head of population; use secondary data to predict the number of people likely to be infected with a flu strain or to experience medication side effects; apply the concept of Indigenous Data Sovereignty to critique and evaluate the Australian Government's Closing the Gap report.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Data can be represented in different ways to establish relationships, while considering accuracy and bias
lessons.lesson_focus: Find the five-number summary (minimum, lower quartile Q1, median, upper quartile Q3, maximum) for a numerical data set; calculate the interquartile range IQR = Q3 − Q1; construct a box plot from the five-number summary; interpret each component of the plot and identify outliers using the 1.5 × IQR convention.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Data can be represented in different ways to establish relationships, while considering accuracy and bias
lessons.lesson_focus: Compare two or more distributions for continuous numerical variables using parallel box plots; discuss shape (symmetry, skew, modality), centre and spread; use digital tools to compare box plots with histograms, cumulative frequency graphs and dot plots of the same data; comment on which display answers a given statistical question most effectively.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Data can be represented in different ways to establish relationships, while considering accuracy and bias
lessons.lesson_focus: Construct a scatterplot from a bivariate data set; describe the association between the two numerical variables in terms of direction (positive, negative, none), strength (strong, moderate, weak) and linearity (linear, non-linear); investigate the relationship between two variables of spear throwers used by Australian First Nations Peoples and construct a scatterplot to compare and draw conclusions.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Data can be represented in different ways to establish relationships, while considering accuracy and bias
lessons.lesson_focus: Informally draw a line of good fit by eye on a scatterplot; use the line to make predictions and discuss the reliability of those predictions (interpolation versus extrapolation); use statistical evidence to make, justify and critique claims about association between variables in contexts such as climate change, migration, online shopping and social media; distinguish association from cause-and-effect.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Data can be represented in different ways to establish relationships, while considering accuracy and bias
lessons.lesson_focus: Construct two-way tables to record responses to questions involving categorical variables — e.g. a five-point Likert-scale survey crossed against junior versus senior respondents; use percentages and proportions within rows and columns to identify patterns and possible associations between the categorical variables; conduct a school-context investigation such as a litter survey crossed with day-of-week or weather.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Data can be represented in different ways to establish relationships, while considering accuracy and bias
lessons.lesson_focus: Plan and conduct a full bivariate statistical investigation — design a study that collects bivariate data over time via observation, experiment or measurement; graph, interpret and analyse the data; report findings with explicit acknowledgement of limitations including interpolation and extrapolation; investigate contexts such as the vaccines-immunity relationship, anecdotal claims about climate or housing affordability, and biodiversity changes in Australia before and after colonisation.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Conditional probability can be described and interpreted for multiple events and applied in real-life contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Interpret conditional statements using the language of probability — "if A then B", "the probability of A given B", "of those who…", "knowing that"; use two-way tables and Venn diagrams to read off conditional probabilities directly; identify common mistakes in conditional language (P(A|B) versus P(B|A) confusion).

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: Conditional probability can be described and interpreted for multiple events and applied in real-life contexts
lessons.lesson_focus: Use arrays and tree diagrams to represent, interpret and compare probabilities of dependent and independent events; recognise when two events are independent (P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B)) versus dependent (multiply along branch but probability changes between stages); contrast with-replacement (independent) and without-replacement (dependent) scenarios.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The likelihood of an event occurring can be affected by another event that has already taken place
lessons.lesson_focus: Use digital simulations to draw samples of different sizes with and without replacement from a known population; identify the sample size at which the difference between with- and without-replacement methods becomes negligible (rule of thumb: population at least 10× sample size); recognise how event dependence affects the way probability is calculated.

lessons.sa_conceptual_understanding: The likelihood of an event occurring can be affected by another event that has already taken place
lessons.lesson_focus: Use simulations to gather data on counter-intuitive probability situations — the Monty Hall (three-door) problem and the birthday problem; identify situations in real life where probability simulations support decision-making such as queueing theory, insurance risk pricing and supply-and-demand for a product; use simulation to predict the number of people likely to be infected with a flu strain or virus.
